data.gender_notes: Suresh is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit word ‘शुर’, Shur, which means a man of valor or hero. The name Suresh signifies one who is secure or victorious in the battles of life. The name Suresh carries the meaning “Secure, Victorious” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Suresh usually hope their child will grow to embody secure, victorious and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Suresh belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Secure, Victorious.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Suresh total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

Hindu mythology is filled with tales of brave warriors and heroes, and the name 'Suresh' is a reminder of this rich cultural heritage. This name is popular among Hindus and has been passed down through generations, reflecting the pride and honor associated with it.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name 'Suresh' implies the realization of the divine within oneself. It symbolizes the victory of the soul over the self and the material world. According to Hindu beliefs, every individual is on a spiritual journey towards self-realization, and the name 'Suresh' is a constant reminder of this goal. data.spiritual_symbolism: Suresh means 'having the certainty of God's blessings'. It symbolizes an unwavering faith in the divine and a life imbued with the confidence of God's grace.

vedic_reference.note: The name Suresh is derived from the Sanskrit words 'shura' and 'ish', meaning 'victorious' and 'lord' respectively.

historical_references.reference: Suresh Qureshi was a prominent Indian politician who served as a Member of Parliament from 1991 to 2004.
historical_references.context: He was a member of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and represented the Maharashtra state in the Lok Sabha, the lower house of the Indian Parliament.

historical_references.reference: Suresh Chanderpant was a Hindu philosopher who lived in the 13th century during the Bhakti movement in India. He was known for his devotion to Lord Vishnu and wrote numerous hymns and poems in Sanskrit.
historical_references.context: His works include the 'Sesha Samhita', a text that explores the nature of God, the soul, and the universe. He is also believed to have influenced the development of the Vaishnavite tradition within Hinduism.
